items.headline: Tech Sell-off Drags S&P 500 and Nasdaq Lower, Dow Posts Marginal Gain
items.summary: U.S. stock markets closed predominantly lower today as concerns mounted over the sustainability of artificial intelligence (AI) spending and rising crude oil prices. The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite experienced its worst single-day performance since early June, while the S&P 500 also tumbled. The Dow Jones Industrial Average, however, managed a slight gain amid the broader market jitters.

items.headline: Meta Platforms falls despite strong earnings amid AI spending concerns
items.summary: Meta Platforms Inc. ($META) stock declined significantly following strong Q3 earnings, as investors expressed concerns over the outlook for AI capital expenditures and return on investment.

items.headline: Tesla drops after reducing CAPEX guidance
items.summary: Tesla ($TSLA) shares fell after the company reduced its full-year capital expenditure guidance by 20%, contributing to broader AI-related market anxieties.

items.headline: AI Trade Plunges Amid Spending Sustainability Doubts
items.summary: The artificial intelligence (AI) trade plummeted today, with market participants deeply concerned about the sustainability of gigantic spending on AI data centers and the potential returns on these investments. This skepticism led to a broad-based sell-off across the AI ecosystem, dragging down tech and semiconductor stocks.

items.headline: Oil Prices Surge on Middle East Tensions, Inflating Market Jitters
items.summary: Crude oil prices surged today, with Brent crude climbing above $114 a barrel, reaching a five-month high. The rally is attributed to escalating Middle East tensions and concerns over potential disruptions to energy supplies, significantly denting overall investor sentiment and raising inflation worries.

items.headline: Energy and Information Technology Lead, Communication Services Lags
items.summary: Amid the mixed market, the Energy sector saw strong performance, driven by rising oil prices, and the Information Technology Select Sector SPDR (XLK) rose 1.7%. Conversely, the Communication Services Select Sector SPDR (XLC) fell 1.1%, reflecting the broader tech downturn.

items.headline: Mixed Economic Data: Jobless Claims Fall, Consumer Sentiment Dips
items.summary: New economic data showed initial jobless claims decreased to 194,000 for the week ended October 17, falling below expectations. However, the University of Michigan's consumer sentiment index for October was revised slightly higher but remained near a five-month low, reflecting ongoing concerns about the economy.

items.headline: Senator Wyden Unveils Proposals for AI Disruption and Data Centers
items.summary: Senator Ron Wyden, Ranking Member of the Senate Finance Committee, introduced new proposals today to address the economic impacts of the AI boom. The legislation aims to enhance unemployment insurance for displaced workers and eliminate federal tax breaks for data center construction, seeking to ensure fair contributions from the industry.
